translationRepairs: Jue Luo Wu Mone, Shu Lan, La Xi, Wangzhar son of La Xi, Sun Boling'a, Tulichen, and He Guozong
Jue Luo Wu Mone, Shu Lan, La Xi, Wangzhar son of La Xi, Boling'a the grandson, Tulichen, and He Guozong
In the chapter head-list, 拉錫子旺札爾孫博靈阿 pairs 子 and 孫 as kinship markers before personal names; 孫 is grandson, not the Chinese surname Sun. The proposed idiomatic correctly yields Boling'a the grandson.
Jue Luo Wu Mone, Shu Lan, La Xi, Wangzhar son of La Xi, Sun Boling'a, Tulichen, and He Guozong
Jue Luo Wu Mone, Shu Lan, La Xi, Wangzhar son of La Xi, Boling'a the grandson, Tulichen, and He Guozong
The same head-list uses 孫 as kinship parallel to 子; rendering 孫博靈阿 as Sun Boling'a invents a surname. Boling'a the grandson matches the Chinese.
His grandson Sun Boling'a inherited the family rank.
His grandson Boling'a inherited the family rank.
s0110 孫博靈阿，襲世職 already marks 孫 as grandson; adding English Sun as a surname is double-counting and false. His grandson Boling'a is accurate and natural.
His grandson Sun Boling'a inherited the hereditary rank.
His grandson Boling'a inherited the hereditary rank.
Literal likewise turns kinship 孫 into a surname; removing Sun leaves His grandson Boling'a, which tracks 孫博靈阿 and 襲世職.
Dzungar taiji Tsewang Arabtan feuded with Ayuki; unable to return, Alabuzhur sought entry at the border, was enfeoffed as beile, and was given pasture outside Jiayu Pass at Dangse'erteng.
Dzungar taiji Tsewang Arabtan feuded with Ayuki; unable to return, Alabuzhur sought entry at the border, was enfeoffed as beizi, and was given pasture outside Jiayu Pass at Dangse'erteng.
詔封貝子 is the Qing rank beizi; beile would require 貝勒. The proposed swap corrects a real title error and leaves the rest of the sentence intact.

The Dzungar taiji Tsewang Arabtan bore a grudge against Ayuki; Alabuzhur could not return, came to the border seeking subject status, was enfeoffed as a beile, and granted pasture outside Jiayu Pass at Dangse'erteng.

The Dzungar taiji Tsewang Arabtan bore a grudge against Ayuki; Alabuzhur could not return, came to the border seeking subject status, was enfeoffed as a beizi, and granted pasture outside Jiayu Pass at Dangse'erteng.
The literal likewise misreads 貝子 as beile; beizi is the correct English for that rank.
On New Year's Day of the sixth year they reached Manuotohai; Ayuki chose a day to receive the edict.
On the first day of the sixth month they reached Manuotohai; Ayuki chose a day to receive the edict.

After 五十三年四月 and 五月, 六年朔 cannot be New Year of a sixth year. Wikisource and CText preserve the received graph 六年朔, but 朔 is a month-day marker and the month-by-month itinerary requires the first day of the sixth month (六月朔); Tulichen's 異域錄 itinerary likewise places arrival at Manuotohai on 六月初一.
On New Year's Day of the sixth year they reached Manuotohai; Ayuki chose a day to hear the edict proclaimed.
On the first day of the sixth month they reached Manuotohai; Ayuki chose a day to hear the edict proclaimed.

CText's Qingshi Gao chapter likewise reads 六年朔 after the fifth-month crossing; as with the idiomatic, that received 年 is a corruption of 月 in context, and first day of the sixth month is the only coherent translation.
